card-model.instruction:
Read docs/TASK_P1_cards.md FIRST: section 2.2 is the contract (the types of src/cards/types.ts verbatim, every fault message as an exact string, the order of faults), section 2.3 the names, section 4 the constraints. docs/CONVENTIONS.md is the style of the tree.

Write three files and nothing else: src/cards/types.ts (exactly the types of section 2.2, no values), src/cards/model.ts (validateCard(input: unknown): CardResult and loadDeck(text: string): DeckResult, importing its types with `import type { ... } from "./types.js"`, node:path for normalisation, no node:fs, no process, no Date), and tests/cards/model.test.ts, a SMOKE test only: at most five test(...) calls (an import, one happy path per function on tests/fixtures/decks/tiny.json via fixture() from ../helpers.js, one tolerant case), toBe on scalars and short strings. The judge writes the example tests, not you. Every message string in the table of section 2.2 is copied exactly, the key order of faults is the schema order, and all faults come back at once.

card-model-judge.instruction: You write tests/cards/model.examples.test.ts only. Import validateCard and loadDeck from "../../src/cards/model.js", types from "../../src/cards/types.js", and fixture/fixtureJson from "../helpers.js"; the fixtures named in section 2.1 of docs/TASK_P1_cards.md hold every example's input (tests/fixtures/cards/*.json for single cards, tests/fixtures/decks/*.json for decks). One test(...) per example below, in this order, named `<Function> example <n>`; then at most twelve tests of your own on the rules of section 2.2. Compare faults as faults.length, faults[0].key and faults[0].message with toBe against the exact strings of section 2.2; narrow a CardResult with `if (!r.ok) ...` and fail with expect.unreachable, never with a cast. Write no file anywhere (loadDeck takes text, not a path).
